differences.what: T-2564: the north return is laid in large dressed courses (about 0.46 m) with staggered joints, 5.5 m long as the course counts in the 1887-89 and 1948 views give it, where it was a smooth 2.8 m slab.

T-2564: the pinnacle caps are ogival with a moulded collar and ball finial, the rear one seated on the coping, and the rounded coping sweeps up into the corner pinnacle on the return and at both front corners.
Most of Keith is occluded by Glessner or outside this frame. Its bow, stair, lower ornament and rear cannot be accepted from this view. The isolated render does not include the occluding neighbour.
T-2579: the camera is re-fitted to Keith's own slice (both pinnacle apexes and three lattice-opening jambs): RMS 0.9 px. With it, what remains is the building and its placement, below.
The original is monochrome; granite colour is not shown. Sepia/scan casts are not material colour.

T-2578 ruling: the stone parapet stops at the rear pinnacle. Every picture that sees that corner (1887, Taylor 2135, the 1888 Glessner plate, the c. 1888 view looking SW, the Glessner front, 1948) shows sky straight behind it, or in 1948 a darker wall about a course lower; the model drops it there.

T-2577: the cornice box under the lattice is laid in the front's dressed stone, so the crown reads as one stone mass from the wall head to the lattice, as the photographs show it; the brown band is gone in this render.

T-2578, re-read at T-2579's camera (0.9 px): the ventilator's cap and the hall stack's top stand clear over the return's coping in the render, where the print shows clean sky over it; with the camera's residual ruled out, either they stand too tall or too far forward for this picture, or the picture (undated here) postdates the ventilator. T-2712: the hall stack's half of this is fixed (it now stops under the coping and the render shows none over it); the cap's top over the coping stays open. T-2713: ruled by the picture's date. Through this 0.74 px camera no cowl inside the record's bounds hides behind the return's coping: at the 0.6 m set-back the cap clears the return's skyline by 45-129 px across the whole 0.4-1.6 m height range, and only at the 1.5 m limit with the cap at 0.95 m or lower does it fall behind, and then against the front's crown, not the return. The c. 1888 view looking SW, the 1887 construction view, Taylor 2135 and the 1888 Glessner plate all show the cowl standing clear, and by Florian 1948 only a stub is left at its foot. This picture is undated, read as probably 1890s-1920s (T-2216, from the front door), so it is taken as later than the cowl's removal: the 1886 phase keeps the cowl and this view cannot show it. T-2811: re-rendered at the cowl's 0.45 m set-back; the cap still clears the return's skyline here, so the ruling by the picture's date stands.

T-2579: the north-east corner pier is wider than the model's: with the lattice jambs and the pinnacles in register, the photograph's arris (front meets return) stands 23 px, about 0.3 m, further north than the model's, the pinnacle standing on the middle of the pier rather than at its arris. T-2680 re-read: there is no edge at x 156. A column profile of the print finds the arris, where the lit front meets the shaded return, at x 138 on every row from the coping (y 80) down to the band (y 360), and none further north; the model's arris projects at x 135-136, 2-3 px (0.03-0.04 m) away, inside the reading. The pinnacle's apex stands 8.5 px inside the arris here and 8 px in the render. Florian 1948 agrees: the plain pier reads 0.37-0.42 m from the lattice's end to the arris there and 0.37 m here, against the model's 0.33 m. The pier stands as the print shows it, so nothing was widened.

T-2579: the lattice openings sit lower, under a deeper coping that sweeps up into the pinnacle (photograph's rows at y 101-113 and 133-146 under a coping near y 70; the render's at 65-82 and 93-110 under one near y 52), and the carved boss at the pier's foot (y 155-180) is missing; the Florian record has the band below. T-2679: the openings are 0.27 m under a 0.32 m head and the boss is built; the rows now read at about y 95-112 and 125-142 against the photograph's 101-113 and 133-146. Still open: the stack between the lower row and the band reads deeper in the render than here, and this camera, fitted to the two pinnacle apexes alone in height, cannot place it apart from Keith's height against Glessner, which T-2680 re-solves. T-2680: read in metres through Florian 1948's camera (fitted to a third-storey light as well) and this one, the lattice stood 0.2-0.23 m too high over the moulded course, so the crown is 0.2 m lower and the course stays level with the boss. Here the boss now reads at y 158-185 against the photograph's 152-178 (y 168-200 before) and the head band at y 280-290 against 265-282 (296-302 before). Still open: about 15 px (0.2 m) of that stack remains deeper in the render than in this print. Florian and the 1888 Keith plate now hold to 2-5 px, so the rest belongs to this camera's height, which only the two pinnacle apexes fix. T-2771: ruled, and it is not this camera: the stack is Keith's, so it stays open as a build (T-2751 carries it). Every camera here is level, and under a level camera a vertical line on the front images evenly, so on one column the stack's length over the lattice's own 0.40 m row pitch is a ratio no eye height, distance or focal length can change (tools/keith_crown_stack.py; docs/RESEARCH/photo-match/keith_house_1808_prairie/a18-gh-glessner-front-with-keith-stack.json). Read on x 15-95, the sills stand at y 115 and 145 in print and render alike, and the head band's top at y 263 against the render's 278: the stack is 3.93 pitches here against the model's 4.35, 1.57 m against 1.74 m (1.55 m through this camera's 76 px/m, which the print's own pitch, 75 px/m, confirms). A tilted camera would need about 45 degrees of pitch to make it, and would lean the north arris 173 px over the crown, where the print holds it at x 138 on every row. Florian 1948 reads the same way, by less: 4.11 pitches, 1.64 m, 4 px at its 45 px/m, which T-2680's 'rows within 3-5 px' had taken as its camera's residual. The 1888 Keith plate cannot rule: on its clearest column (x 520-540) the branches leave its ratio anywhere in 3.3-4.8. Florian places the excess between the lattice's sill and the checker band (0.41 m in print against the model's 0.62 m); here the moulded course's shadow hides the band's first row. T-2813: built. The moulded course under the lattice is 0.20 m deep where it was 0.36 m, and the wall head and everything over it stand 0.16 m lower, with the checker band and head band left where they were; the camera is re-solved on the moved pinnacle apexes (0.74 px RMS, as before). On x 15-95 the render's sills now read at y 115 and 145.5 against the print's 115 and 145, and the head band's top (the foot of the lit plain ground) at y 265.5 against 263, where it read 278: the stack is 3.95 pitches against the print's 3.93, 1.58 m against 1.57 (tools/keith_crown_stack.py), within about 2 px. Florian 1948 reads the same stack 1.3 px short through its re-solved camera.

T-2579: Keith's slice and Glessner's front do not fit one level camera as the two models are placed: the Keith-only fit puts Glessner's north-east corner 54 px aside and 71 px low (its Taylor-fit corners, translated), and no level camera holds both buildings within 20 px (best joint RMS 22 px). So Keith's height or set-back relative to Glessner differs from the placement, which is the relative-height question this view was kept for. T-2680: it is the camera, not the placement. The fit held the principal point at x 584. Freed, Keith's five controls and Glessner's north-east eave corner hold one level camera within 1.6 px (cx 671, f 2492). The grade corner read at y 1265 is the top of the parkway curb in front of Glessner, which hides the building's foot: the joint fit puts the foot at y 1294, behind that curb (y 1258-1295). The eave reading itself sits on the downpipe's leader head, so it is a weak control, and this print gives no evidence that Keith's height or set-back against Glessner differs from the placement.

T-2714: the checker band's units are pitched 0.28 m along their rows (0.336 m before), with 0.07 m of ground between neighbours, as the 1888 Keith plate lays them; the rows are unchanged. Not judged here: Keith's front is edge-on behind the return; the band's units are not resolved.

T-2876: re-rendered on the GLB in the tree, T-2845's loggia (0.6 m pedestals at the first-floor plan's place, each pair's shafts 0.36 m apart, the flight 1.8 m clear and the stoop 0.15 m south), and read again beside the previous render and the picture: the render changes only at Keith's loggia (x 12-316), which this picture shows behind Glessner's front and a street tree; the capital and pair it shows sit on the render's within the tree's cover, and nothing behind them is visible. T-2882: re-rendered on the loggia with a respond on the wall behind each rear pair (a flat pier the rear pedestal's width, 0.25 m deep, from the pedestal's top to the ceiling; tools/keith_loggia_respond_read.py, docs/RESEARCH/photo-match/keith_house_1808_prairie/keith-loggia-respond-read.json), and read again beside the previous render and the picture: the render changes only at the loggia (x 88-134, y 904-1064); the rear row stands behind the respond's face, and this picture does not read the rear row, for the reason T-2881's item above gives, so it does not read the respond either. Nothing it shows opens a difference; the verdict stands (matches).

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236).
